1.title: Actions for CI
1.text: Welcome to Module fourteen: Actions for C I. It covers the exam area Part five: Automation and safety. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Build and test a Node and a Python project in a workflow. Run a matrix with include, exclude and fail-fast. Cache dependencies. Share files between jobs with artifacts. Use secrets, variables and environments. Set least-privilege permissions. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Course
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the course. Part: Part five: Automation and safety. Verified with: the Git Hub documentation (read twenty twenty-six-eleven to sixteen); workflow files checked for syntax, not run.

1.title: What Was Executed and What Is Reference Only
1.text: What Was Executed and What Is Reference Only. Workflow files run on Git Hub and were not run there. They were checked for syntax and against Git Hub's workflow schema, and the shell commands in them were run locally.

1.title: A CI workflow: build and test on every change
1.text: A C I workflow: build and test on every change. Continuous integration (C I) means that every push and pull request is built and tested automatically, so a broken change shows up before it is merged. The figure shows the pipeline from a push to a green or red check.

1.title: A CI workflow: build and test on every change, continued
1.text: A C I workflow: build and test on every change. The figure shows this: A push or pull request starts the C I workflow: checkout, set up the language, restore the cache, install, test, then a green or red check on the pull request.

1.title: A CI workflow: build and test on every change, continued
1.text: A C I workflow: build and test on every change. A C I job has the same shape for every language: get the code, set up the language, install, test. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: A CI workflow: build and test on every change, continued
1.text: A C I workflow: build and test on every change. Set up. Node project: actions slash setup node at v seven with node version. Python project: actions slash setup python at v five with python version. Cache. Node project: cache N P M. Python project: cache pip. Install. Node project: N P M ci. Python project: pip install dash r requirements dot txt. Test. Node project: N P M test. Python project: python dash m unittest. Action versions move on. The ones above are the major versions in the official examples when this course was written, so check each action's releases page before you copy one. Tip: Quote Python versions in yammel. An unquoted three dot ten is read as the number three point one, so the job would install the wrong Python.

1.title: Matrix, cache and artifacts
1.text: Matrix, cache and artifacts. A matrix runs one job definition many times with different values, for example two operating systems and two Python versions. matrix. Every combination of the listed values becomes its own job. exclude. Removes one combination. include. Adds one more combination, for example mac O S with Python three point one three. fail-fast. True by default: the first failure cancels the other jobs; false lets all finish. max-parallel. Limits how many matrix jobs run at once.

1.title: Matrix, cache and artifacts, continued
1.text: Matrix, cache and artifacts. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Matrix, cache and artifacts, continued
1.text: Matrix, cache and artifacts. Two operating systems times two versions gives four combinations. The exclude removes one, so three jobs run. Caching saves the time of downloading dependencies again. The easy way is cache N P M or cache pip in the setup action. By hand, use actions slash cache with a path, a key of at most five hundred twelve characters and optional restore keys.

1.title: Matrix, cache and artifacts, continued
1.text: Matrix, cache and artifacts. Hit. The exact key was found, and the step output cache hit is true. Immutable. A cache never changes; to refresh it, change the key, for example with a hash of the lock file. Eviction. Entries not used for seven days are removed; the default limit is ten gigabytes per repository. Scope. Per branch: a pull request uses the merge ref, and sibling branches cannot share.

1.title: Matrix, cache and artifacts, continued
1.text: Matrix, cache and artifacts. An artifact is different: it moves files out of a job, to a later job or to a person. Upload with actions slash upload artifact ( name, path, retention days ) and download with actions slash download artifact. Jobs run on separate machines, so the consuming job must list the producer in needs. Version four artifacts are immutable, and they share storage with Packages.

1.title: Matrix, cache and artifacts, continued
1.text: Matrix, cache and artifacts. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Tip: Never make a build depend on a cache hit. A cache is a speed-up that can be missing; an artifact is the result of this run.

1.title: Secrets, variables and environments
1.text: Secrets, variables and environments. Repository secrets are saved in Settings, Secrets and variables, Actions. Organizations can hold secrets too, and so can an environment: a named target such as staging or production that a job selects with environment. Secret. How a workflow reads it: secrets dot name in with or env. Rules: Never on the command line; an unset secret is an empty string. Variable. How a workflow reads it: vars dot name. Rules: Plain configuration, not for secrets. github token. How a workflow reads it: secrets dot github token. Rules: Made for each job; ends when the job ends.

1.title: Secrets, variables and environments, continued
1.text: Secrets, variables and environments. Secrets are not given to workflows triggered from forks (only the read-only token is) or by Depend a bot. A secret also cannot be used directly in an if. Copy it into a job-level env variable and test that variable instead, as the called workflow in section five does. Tip: To test whether a secret exists, put it in a job-level env and write if env dot token!. A condition that names secrets dot token directly does not work.

1.title: Permissions, concurrency, filters and the merge queue
1.text: Permissions, concurrency, filters and the merge queue. Permissions. Set permissions to limit what github token can do: read, write or none for each scope, such as contents. If you set any scope, every scope you leave out becomes none. The shorthands are read all, write all and (nothing). Use least privilege: read contents at the top of the file and raise one job only when it needs more.

1.title: Permissions, concurrency, filters and the merge queue, continued
1.text: Permissions, concurrency, filters and the merge queue. concurrency group. Only one run per group at a time, for example one per branch. cancel-in-progress. Off by default; true cancels the running run when a newer one starts. paths, paths-ignore. Run only when the changed files match (a skipped required check stays Pending). merge group. The event of a merge queue; type checks requested.

2.title: Permissions, concurrency, filters and the merge queue, continued
2.text: Permissions, concurrency, filters and the merge queue. A merge queue merges pull requests into a busy protected branch in order. Each pull request is tested against the latest target branch plus the pull requests queued before it. If a required check must run for the queue, its workflow must also listen to merge group. Tip: Set cancel in progress true on a branch group. Three quick pushes then cost one finished run instead of three.

2.title: Reusable workflows
2.text: Reusable workflows. A reusable workflow is a workflow other workflows can call. The called file sits in dot github slash workflows and starts with on workflow call, which can declare inputs (boolean, number or string), secrets and outputs. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

2.title: Reusable workflows, continued
2.text: Reusable workflows. The caller uses the file at job level with uses, not as a step, and hands over with and secrets (or secrets inherit inside one organization or enterprise). The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

2.title: Reusable workflows, continued
2.text: Reusable workflows. Path forms. . slash dot github slash workflows slash file dot yml or owner slash repo slash dot github slash workflows slash file dot yml at ref; a commit S H A is safest. Nesting. Up to ten levels. Permissions. A called workflow can keep or lower them, never raise them.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. A matrix has os ubuntu latest, windows latest and python three dot twelve, three dot thirteen, plus one exclude for Windows with three point one two. How many jobs run? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Three, because exclude removes one of four combinations. The matrix makes four combinations and the exclude entry removes one of them.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. A cache step uses the fixed key N P M cache. The lock file changed, but the install still shows the old packages. Why? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Caches are immutable, so the same key restores old files. Caches are immutable, so a new key (for example with a hash of the lock file) is needed to refresh one.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. A step has if secrets dot token!, and the run reports an error. What is the correct fix? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Copy it into a job-level env variable and test that. A secret cannot be used directly in an if, but a job-level env variable that holds it can.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. A workflow sets only permissions contents read at the top. A step then tries to comment on a pull request with the token and is refused. Why? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Setting any scope turns every unlisted scope to none. Once one scope is set, every scope that is left out becomes none, so the job needs pull requests write.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Three pushes in a minute start three C I runs on one branch, and only the last one matters. What should you add? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A concurrency group per branch with cancel in progress true. Concurrency allows one run per group, and cancel-in-progress stops the older run when a newer one starts.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. A caller workflow has - uses. slash dot github slash workflows slash deploy dot yml as a step, and the run fails. What is the fix? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Move uses to the job level, as in jobs dot stage dot uses. A reusable workflow is called with uses on the job, never as a step.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the default of fail fast in a matrix? Answer: True: the first failure cancels the other jobs. Question two. How long can a cache entry go unused before it is evicted? Answer: seven days. Question three. Which key must a job add to use an artifact made by another job? Answer: needs, naming the producer job.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which trigger declares a reusable workflow? Answer: on workflow call. Question five. Which event must a workflow listen to so its checks run in a merge queue? Answer: merge group. Question six. What does permissions do? Answer: It gives the token no permissions at all.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. C I job: checkout, set up the language, install, test; cache N P M or cache pip. Matrix: matrix makes combinations; exclude removes, include adds; fail fast true by default. Cache: key up to five hundred twelve characters; immutable; evicted after seven days; ten gigabytes per repository. Artifacts: upload artifact and download artifact; the consumer needs the producer. Secrets: secrets dot name in with or env; never directly in if; none for forks. Permissions: set one scope and the rest become none; start with read contents. Concurrency: group plus cancel in progress (off by default). Reuse: workflow call with inputs, secrets, outputs; caller uses uses at job level.
